column3: MT 7:1–2; the following verses of this psalm are MT +1. NASB sets the title in braces before verse 1; “on the words of Cush” is rendered “concerning Cush.”
Close to the Hebrew; “tearing” is rendered “Dragging me away.”
“I have rescued my opposer without cause” is rendered “have plundered him who without cause was my adversary.”
Close to the Hebrew; “my honor” is rendered “my glory.”
Close to the Hebrew; “nations” is rendered “peoples,” and “over it” as “over them.”
Close to the Hebrew; “let Him judge” is rendered “judges.”
NASB restructures the second line as “For the righteous God tries the hearts and minds”; “kidneys” is rendered “minds.”
Close to the Hebrew; “on God” is rendered “with God.”
The subject of “will sharpen” is not named in Hebrew; NASB capitalizes “His sword” and “His bow,” taking God as the subject.
“For him” is rendered “for Himself,” and “into burning ones” as “fiery shafts.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he digs a pit and has dug it” is rendered “He has dug a pit and hollowed it out.”
